item.research_question: How does the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, combined with annealing temperature, influence the hierarchical phase decomposition, microstructure, and resulting magnetic and mechanical properties in AlCoFeNi-based high entropy alloys?
item.material_system: AlCoFeNi (x=1) and AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi (x=0.5) high entropy alloys
item.processing_route: Arc melting of elemental pellets (99.9% purity) under argon atmosphere followed by isothermal annealing at 600 °C and 1000 °C for 15 h and water quenching
item.test_conditions: Annealing at 600 °C/15 h and 1000 °C/15 h; characterization via SEM, EBSD, TEM, APT, Vickers microhardness, and magnetic saturation/coercivity measurements
key_findings: AlCoFeNi annealed at 1000 °C forms a single ordered B2 phase with a microhardness of 406 VHN and saturation magnetization of 112 emu/g.
AlCoFeNi annealed at 600 °C decomposes into a B2 + BCC mixture with a microhardness of 474 VHN.
AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi annealed at 1000 °C exhibits coarse B2 + BCC phase separation with grain boundary FCC phases.
AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi annealed at 600 °C shows a hierarchical microstructure with decomposition length scales ranging from ~3–5 nm (APT) to ~50–100 nm (TEM) to micron-scale lamellae.
The AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy annealed at 600 °C achieved the highest microhardness of 475 VHN.
Saturation magnetization of the Cr-containing alloy (AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi) is reduced by more than 50% compared to the Cr-free alloy due to the antiferromagnetic nature of Cr.
Coercivity decreases with increasing annealing temperature, dropping from 15 Oe at 600 °C to 4 Oe at 1000 °C for the AlCoFeNi alloy.
APT cluster analysis detected Cr-rich BCC precipitates with concentrations ranging from 16% to 74% depending on the generation scale.
item.mechanism: The addition of Cr enhances phase separation due to the positive enthalpy of mixing in Fe-Cr, Co-Cr, and Ni-Cr systems, which creates miscibility gaps, whereas the Al-Cr system has a negative enthalpy of mixing favoring compound formation; the length scale of decomposition is controlled by the interplay of composition and annealing temperature.
item.limitations: The thermodynamic model predicted an FCC phase in AlCoFeNi at 1000 °C which was not observed experimentally, likely due to a high nucleation barrier; the specific thermodynamic basis for Cr's influence on phase separation in these complex multi-component alloys requires further analysis beyond the scope of the paper.
item.future_work: Further detailed investigation is required to understand the relationship between B2 phase decomposition into a two-phase B2 + BCC microstructure and the resulting coercivity; the details of the thermodynamic basis underlying the influence of Cr on phase separation require analysis beyond the current scope.
quotes: The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature.
The strong tendency of Cr to introduce phase separation in the B2 phase can possibly be attributed to a positive enthalpy of mixing of Fe-Cr, Co-Cr and Ni-Cr systems.
